# Breast abscess

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Breast disorders > Breast abscess*

[Original Article Link](/library/Tt0613)

---

## Summary

A <u>breast</u> <u>abscess</u> is an encapsulated accumulation of <u>pus</u> within the <u>breast</u> tissue that most commonly results from <u>puerperal mastitis</u>. Nonpuerperal <u>abscesses</u> are uncommon and may be caused by trauma. <u>Breast</u> <u>abscesses</u> typically manifest as a tender, <u>erythematous</u> <u>breast mass</u> with or without systemic signs of infection, such as <u>fever</u>. The diagnosis is primarily clinical, but imaging and <u>aspiration</u> are often required for confirmation and to guide management. Treatment involves drainage, <u>antibiotics</u>, and <u>analgesia</u>.

---

## Clinical features

* <u>Breast</u> <u>pain</u>, <u>erythema</u>, and <u>edema</u>

* <u>Purulent</u> discharge from the <u>nipple</u> of the affected <u>breast</u>

* <u>Fluctuant</u> mass on palpation

* Possibly overlying <u>skin</u> <u>necrosis</u>

* <u>Fever</u>

* <u>Nausea</u>





> [!TIP]
> A <u>fluctuant</u> <u>breast mass</u> may indicate an <u>abscess</u>.

---

## Treatment

Treatment typically involves drainage, <u>antibiotics</u>, and adequate <u>pain management</u>. Surgical excision may be considered for chronic <u>abscesses</u> or <u>fistulas</u>.  [[2]](/library/bXaH9Q)[[4]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[5]](/library/5R1ing0)




### <u>Abscess</u> drainage  [[8]](/library/pg1LwT0)




* Percutaneous drainage;  : first-line for <u>abscesses</u> with intact overlying <u>skin</u>  [[6]](/library/qh1CUg0)[[9]](/library/iR1J5g0)

* <u>Incision and drainage</u>;   : Consider for multiloculated or large <u>abscesses</u>, <u>necrosis</u> of overlying <u>skin</u>, or failure of percutaenous drainage. [[5]](/library/5R1ing0)[[9]](/library/iR1J5g0)





### <u>Antibiotic</u> treatment [[4]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[5]](/library/5R1ing0)




* See “<u>Empiric antibiotics for breast infections</u>.”

* Tailor therapy based on cultures.





> [!TIP]
> Patients with puerperal <u>abscesses</u> can continue to breastfeed. Patients who have undergone an <u>incision and drainage</u> may consider using a <u>breast</u> pump. [[2]](/library/bXaH9Q)[[5]](/library/5R1ing0)
